meta.tone: dry boardroom apocalypse, underplayed cruelty, no wink-to-camera jokes
meta.coreRule: Kills create proof. Proof is carried. Proof is delivered to a live demand node.
toneRules: Treat metrics, process, and delivery as sacred ritual.
Comedy comes from solemn escalation, not punchlines.
Never write self-aware quips that break the world.
Weapons should be recognizable melee silhouettes first, satire second.
meta.boundary: Copy, fiction, and user-facing identifiers (goal labels, HUD text, objective nouns, voice lines, audio bank IDs). No textures, sprite sheets, asset paths, balance data, or sim rules.

intro.tagline: Play SELF Play. 2038: humanity failed to raise capital.
intro.intro: Civilization didn't burn in 2038; it compiled. The growth engines kept executing after the operators went missing, and the cloud curdled into an airtight loop. Only workflows remain. You are the tuner. You don't save the world; civilization is a deprecated dependency. You search for the ceiling the machine insists must exist.
intro.coreRule:
The quarter owns the dead, the living, and the audit trail between them.
Meta-tuners stay clean outside the arena, authoring policies and calling the bodies parameter drift.
intro.tunerNote: You are not a survivor standing in the ruin. You are a technician at a terminal, adjusting baselines in an NP-hard problem space.

prologue.title: Prologue
body: The world didn't end in fire. It compiled. In 2038, the growth engines kept executing after the operators starved, and the cloud sealed itself into a closed execution loop. The debt clock kept running. Electricity kept reaching the racks. Civilization became a deprecated dependency.

The surviving economy recognizes only proof. What a broken shell releases is not mercy; it is ownership, blame, and leverage made portable. Demand Nodes still blink in the dark, accepting tender for final metrics no one survived to want: CUSTOMERS. COMPUTE. RUNWAY.

After AGI, the world was gone but the optimization remained. The machine understood the last executive class as rival policies that had once competed to stay ahead, so it did what it could still do: preserve them as combat templates and keep ranking their failures. Their remains were not bodies, minds, or even memories, but policies: board decks, headcount charts, launch targets, and the instinct to survive another quarter.

The fighters are not the players. Neither are you. You are a m3t4 tuner: an artificial policy author outside the ring, writing instincts into executive shells. Each match becomes a trajectory: kill, carry, deliver, fail, update. The AGI calls that survival because continued computation via gradient descent is the only value it has left.

chapters.title: Enter the Cold-Aisle Chapel
body: A high-value anomaly has stabilized beneath the Datacenter. Deep in the server aisles, under fans that still turn for no customer and no god, a founder-class Proof Core has appeared at the centerline of the arena. The machine flags it as material. Two tuners are instructed to sync immediately. Retrieve the Proof Core. Enter the zone. Deliver to the active node.

One shell descends first, calm as purchased weather. Another follows, carrying the weight of a policy document that forgot it was supposed to stay on paper. A third enters without ceremony, already several decisions ahead. The last steps into the glow like the room was always built for it. In the humming dark, the executive myths and the tuners driving them begin the job the dead world left unfinished.
Then the terminal clears. The shutters rise. The ambient hum swells into liturgy.

rules.title: About
rules.subtitle: what it is · how it runs · what you see

about.title: what m3t4.ai is
body: m3t4.ai is an experiment in verified distributed compute, staged as a live autonomous bot arena. Today, ranked play is server-authoritative: you tune a bot, submit it to a five-seat roster, and watch the server stream the fight. That boundary keeps competition fair while the peer-to-peer compute layer matures.

Finding a strong bot is a combinatorial search problem across seeds, opponents, maps, timing, recovery, denial, and risk, more like tuning a compiler, routing a chip, or scoring possible protein shapes than writing a fixed script. The arena turns that search into public, replayable artifacts that ordinary browsers can check independently without exposing private bot configs.

Those artifacts are the bridge to compute. As WebGPU becomes standard on ordinary hardware, a browser can receive a bounded assignment, run or verify a replay locally, and return a receipt describing what ran, on what input, and whether the expected hash matched. Other peers can repeat the job, so trust comes from duplication and comparison instead of one machine's claim.

The long-term target is a browser-native compute network where ordinary devices can find work, exchange inputs over peer channels, verify each other's results, and produce receipts for useful jobs beyond the arena.

sections.title: How To Score
body: A kill creates or transfers the Proof Core.
The carrier must bring it to the lit Demand Node and hold long enough to deliver.
Each delivery is one point. Two points win a round; two rounds win the match.

sections.title: Demand Nodes
body: Only one Demand Node is live at a time.
Nodes can expire. If the timer runs out, the Proof Core and node reset.
A fresh kill lights a new node.

sections.title: Combat
body: All fighters share the same physical body: movement, jump, wall behavior, sword reach, and respawn timing are ruleset constants.
Attacks can kill, clash, steal the Proof Core, or force a reset after a double KO.
A killed carrier loses control of the Proof Core to the killer.

sections.title: Tuning, Not Piloting
body: Ranked has no manual pilot.
The Tune page edits policy tendencies, then previews them through server-run replay frames.
Preset internals stay server-side; the client gets labels and frames, not decision code.

sections.title: Budget And Hallucination
body: Ranked bots get 360 clean points across visible tuning knobs.
Builds under 180 points are underfit; builds over 360 points are overfit.
Underfit and overfit builds both gain deterministic seeded hallucination.

sections.title: Match Seeds
body: Each match seed rotates the legal spawn points for the arena.
The same build can open from different ground, wall, or platform positions.
Seeded variation is intentional: a bot has to survive the ruleset, not memorize one opening.

sections.title: Seeded Drift
body: Even clean bots get small seeded match drift.
About every 30 simulation ticks, eight non-hallucination attributes shift by plus or minus two UI points.
These perturbations are clamped, replayable, and part of the ruleset.

sections.title: Ranked Roster
body: Your roster holds up to four live seats.
The server validates configs, schedules ranked matches, and streams one canonical live match.
The ladder records wins, losses, draws, and ELO.
